g.data-timing: 2 x SYNC (BITS/J.211/DTI) RJ-45, IEEE 1588 RJ-45, 2 x nV Sync RJ-45, 10 MHz and 1 PPS SMB
g.title: asr-9922-rp-tr

g.data-description: the nine-pin Alarm Out connector, drawn rather than composed: there is no std/ part for a DE-9 and no registry key for its panel opening, and no document in the intake dimensions it. Declared `class: cutout` all the same - see provenance.db9 for why withholding that was the wrong way round.

rect.data-description: the four-character 5x7 LED dot-matrix display. What it shows is a message vocabulary - the guide gives it two sections, boot-stage/runtime and CAN bus controller errors - not a lamp state list, so it is a display and not an indicator.

circle.data-description: Power Fail (FAIL). Red: standby power fail; the LED is turned off by the CAN bus controller once it is up and running. Off: standby power is normal.
Alarm Cutoff (ACO). Amber: alarm cutoff has been enabled - the ACO push button was pressed after at least one alarm occurred.

Synchronization (SYNC). Table 5, 'RP and RP2/RP3 Discrete LED Display Definitions' - this card's own table, not the RSP family's Table 4, and the two differ here. Green: 'System timing is synchronized to an external timing source INCLUDING IEEE 1588' - Table 4 omits the 1588 clause. Amber: system timing is free running. Off (default after reset): Cisco writes 'LED never turns off', which contradicts listing Off as a colour at all; off is kept as a declared state because the drawing needs an unlit appearance, and Cisco's sentence is recorded here rather than tidied away. Table 4 says 'No system timing is configured' for the same row, which is the RSP family's answer and is not this card's.
Critical Alarm (CRIT). Red: a critical alarm has occurred.
Major Alarm (MAJ). Red: a major alarm has occurred.
Minor Alarm (MIN). Amber: a minor alarm has occurred.
Internal Solid State Hard Disk Drive (SSD). Green: SSD0 is busy/active.

FC Fault. Table 5, 'RP and RP2/RP3 Discrete LED Display Definitions' - amber: 'A fault has occurred on any or all of the FC cards installed. This LED will be on during the boot phase of the FC.' Off (default after reset): 'FC cards are booted up and ready.' A real vocabulary from this card's own table. An earlier version of this component said no row for FC FAULT existed in Table 4 or Table 5 and carried a bare off/on; that was wrong about Table 5.
the LAMP TEST momentary push button.
